label: Bonus Class 2
title: How Stories Are Built: The Story Mountain
bigIdea: Almost every good story, in English or in Arabic, climbs the same mountain: a setting, a problem that grows, a climax, and an ending. Linking words are the ropes that hold the parts together.
bigIdeaAr: كل قصة جيدة تقريباً، بالإنجليزية أو بالعربية، تصعد الجبل نفسه: مكان وزمان، ثم مشكلة تكبر، ثم ذروة، ثم نهاية. وكلمات الربط هي الحبال التي تشدّ الأجزاء معاً.
builtOn: Lessons 1-4: past simple (regular, irregular, did, was/were) and adjectives for feelings and places
Lesson 5: there was / there were (crowd, queue, traffic, ticket, delay, surprise, problem)
Lesson 6: time expressions (yesterday, last week, two days ago, last summer, recently)
Lesson 7: sequencing words (first, then, next, after that, finally, in the end, meanwhile, suddenly, at last)
Lesson 8: reasons and results (because, so, since, therefore, reason, cause, result)

objectives.en: I can name the five parts of the story mountain and find them in a short story.
objectives.ar: أستطيع أن أسمّي الأجزاء الخمسة لجبل القصة وأجدها في قصة قصيرة.

objectives.en: I can open and close a story in English and compare it with Arabic openers like كان يا ما كان.
objectives.ar: أستطيع أن أبدأ قصة وأنهيها بالإنجليزية وأقارنها ببدايات عربية مثل «كان يا ما كان».

objectives.en: I can link my sentences with time words and because / so instead of 'and then... and then'.
objectives.ar: أستطيع أن أربط جملي بكلمات الزمن و because / so بدلاً من «and then... and then».

objectives.en: I can build a short story with my team, one part each.
objectives.ar: أستطيع أن أبني قصة قصيرة مع فريقي، كل واحد يكتب جزءاً.

keyTerms.meaning: The start: who, where, when. 'Last Friday there was a big match...'
The problem starts and grows. Things get harder.
The top of the mountain: the most exciting or scary moment.
What the characters do to fix the problem.
How it ends and how the characters feel.
A word that joins ideas: first, then, suddenly, because, so, in the end.
Stopping a story at the most exciting moment, so the listener wants more.

facts.en: About 2,300 years ago the Greek thinker Aristotle said a story needs a beginning, a middle and an end. In 1863 the German writer Gustav Freytag drew this as a pyramid with five parts. Schools today call it the story mountain.
facts.ar: قبل نحو 2300 سنة قال الفيلسوف اليوناني أرسطو إن القصة تحتاج إلى بداية ووسط ونهاية. وفي عام 1863 رسمها الكاتب الألماني غوستاف فرايتاغ هرماً من خمسة أجزاء، وتسميه المدارس اليوم «جبل القصة».

facts.en: The five parts: setting (who, where, when) - rising action (a problem grows) - climax (the top!) - falling action (fixing it) - resolution (the ending and the feeling).
facts.ar: الأجزاء الخمسة: التمهيد (من، أين، متى) - تصاعد الأحداث (المشكلة تكبر) - الذروة (القمة!) - انحدار الأحداث (حل المشكلة) - الخاتمة (النهاية والشعور).

facts.en: It is not only for books. In the 1960s the linguist William Labov recorded ordinary people telling true stories about their lives. Their stories had the same parts, plus one more: the 'evaluation', the part that says why the story matters ('It was the scariest moment of my life!').
facts.ar: ليس للكتب فقط. في الستينيات سجّل اللغوي ويليام لابوف أشخاصاً عاديين يحكون قصصاً حقيقية من حياتهم، فوجد في قصصهم الأجزاء نفسها، إضافة إلى جزء آخر هو «التقييم»: الجزء الذي يقول لماذا القصة مهمة.

facts.en: Linking words do a special job that linguists call cohesion: they glue sentences together and tell the listener what comes next. 'Suddenly' warns: a surprise is coming. 'So' shows a result. 'In the end' says: the story is closing.
facts.ar: تقوم كلمات الربط بعمل يسميه اللغويون «التماسك»: تلصق الجمل ببعضها وتخبر السامع بما سيأتي. Suddenly تنبّه إلى مفاجأة، و so تُظهر نتيجة، و in the end تقول إن القصة تُختم.

facts.en: Every culture has story formulas: 'Once upon a time' in English, 'كان يا ما كان، في قديم الزمان' in Arabic. They are signals: they tell the listener 'relax, a story is starting'.
facts.ar: لكل ثقافة صيغ ثابتة للحكاية: Once upon a time بالإنجليزية، و«كان يا ما كان، في قديم الزمان» بالعربية. إنها إشارات تقول للسامع: «استرخِ، الحكاية بدأت».

facts.en: The most famous cliffhangers in the world are Arabic: in 'One Thousand and One Nights', Shahrazad stops every night at the exciting part, so the king wants to hear the rest tomorrow.
facts.ar: أشهر النهايات المعلّقة في العالم عربية: في «ألف ليلة وليلة» تتوقف شهرزاد كل ليلة عند الجزء المثير، فيريد الملك أن يسمع البقية في الليلة التالية.

arabicBridge.english: Once upon a time... / A long time ago...
arabicBridge.arabic: كان يا ما كان، في قديم الزمان، وسالف العصر والأوان
arabicBridge.point: Both languages have a fixed, magical opener for folk tales. English is short; the Arabic one is longer and has rhyme and rhythm. For a true personal story, English starts with a time phrase: 'Last summer...', 'Two days ago...'.
arabicBridge.pointAr: في اللغتين بداية ثابتة سحرية للحكايات الشعبية. الإنجليزية قصيرة، والعربية أطول وفيها سجع وإيقاع. وللقصة الشخصية الحقيقية تبدأ الإنجليزية بعبارة زمن مثل Last summer.

arabicBridge.arabic: وعاشوا في تبات ونبات، وخلّفوا صبيان وبنات (خاتمة مصرية شعبية)
arabicBridge.point: Fixed endings exist in both. In modern stories English usually ends with a feeling or a lesson: 'In the end, we were tired but happy.'
arabicBridge.pointAr: توجد خواتيم ثابتة في اللغتين. وفي القصص الحديثة تنتهي الإنجليزية غالباً بشعور أو درس: In the end, we were tired but happy.

arabicBridge.english: then / after that / suddenly / so / because
arabicBridge.arabic: و / فـ / ثم / فجأةً / لذلك / لأنّ
arabicBridge.point: Arabic grammar already knows the difference: فـ means 'then, right away' and ثم means 'then, after some time'. English shows this with different words: then, immediately, after that, later. Arabic writing often joins many sentences with و; in English a long chain of 'and... and then...' sounds childish. Use full stops and different linking words.
arabicBridge.pointAr: النحو العربي يعرف الفرق أصلاً: الفاء للترتيب والتعقيب، وثم للترتيب والتراخي. والإنجليزية تُظهر ذلك بكلمات مختلفة: then و after that و later. الكتابة العربية تربط جملاً كثيرة بالواو، أما في الإنجليزية فسلسلة and then الطويلة تبدو طفولية. استخدم النقطة وكلمات ربط متنوعة.

arabicBridge.point: Arabic puts قبل BEFORE the time; English puts ago AFTER it: two days ago (not 'before two days'). And 'last week' needs no preposition (not 'in last week').
arabicBridge.pointAr: العربية تضع «قبل» قبل المدة، والإنجليزية تضع ago بعدها: two days ago وليس before two days. و last week لا تحتاج إلى حرف جر (وليس in last week).

arabicBridge.english: Because there was traffic, we were late. / There was traffic, so we were late.
arabicBridge.arabic: لأنه كان هناك زحام، تأخرنا. / كان هناك زحام، لذلك تأخرنا.
arabicBridge.point: Use ONE linker: because OR so, not both. Arabic can say «لأنني كنت متعباً فنمت» with فـ in the second half, but English cannot say 'Because I was tired, so I slept'.
arabicBridge.pointAr: استخدم أداة ربط واحدة: because أو so وليس الاثنتين. العربية تقول «لأنني كنت متعباً فنمت» بالفاء في النصف الثاني، لكن الإنجليزية لا تقبل Because I was tired, so I slept.

commonErrors.wrong: Before two days I went to the mall.
commonErrors.right: Two days ago I went to the mall.
commonErrors.why: Direct translation of قبل يومين. In English, ago comes after the time.

commonErrors.wrong: In last week we visited my uncle.
commonErrors.right: Last week we visited my uncle.
commonErrors.why: Translating في الأسبوع الماضي word by word. last / next / this + time take no preposition.

commonErrors.wrong: There was many people in the queue.
commonErrors.right: There were many people in the queue.
commonErrors.why: In Arabic كان هناك stays the same; in English it must agree: was + one, were + many.

commonErrors.wrong: Because I was tired, so I went to bed.
commonErrors.right: Because I was tired, I went to bed. / I was tired, so I went to bed.
commonErrors.why: Using two linkers, influenced by Arabic لأنّ... فـ. English takes one.

commonErrors.wrong: We went to the mall and then we ate and then we saw a film and then we went home.
commonErrors.right: First, we went to the mall. After that, we ate. Then we saw a film. In the end, we went home.
commonErrors.why: Long و-style chains. English prefers shorter sentences with varied linking words.

commonErrors.wrong: We were late because the traffic.
commonErrors.right: We were late because of the traffic. / ...because there was a lot of traffic.
commonErrors.why: because + a sentence (subject + verb); because of + a noun.

teacher: Story mountain diagram (five flags on a mountain)
The Lost Ticket story (Hamad and Omar) on a slide
Story Dice cards on a slide: Setting / Problem / Twist / Ending
A shared whiteboard (Teams Whiteboard) for the chain story
student: A drawn mountain with five flags (they draw it in Stage 2)

stages.name: Warm-up: Which Language Is This Opener?
stages.purpose: Show that story formulas are universal and switch on 'story mode'.
teacherSays: Story Scientists, listen: 'كان يا ما كان، في قديم الزمان...' What happens next? A story! How do you know? Those words are a signal.
English has a signal too: 'Once upon a time...' What kind of story starts like that? A fairy tale!
And a true story from your life? You do not say 'once upon a time'. You say: 'Last Friday...', 'Two days ago...'.
Quick round: start a true story with a time phrase in 10 seconds. Go!
teacherSaysAr: «كان يا ما كان» إشارة تقول: الحكاية بدأت. وفي الإنجليزية Once upon a time للحكايات الخيالية.
أما القصة الحقيقية من حياتك فتبدأ بعبارة زمن: Last Friday أو Two days ago.
studentsDo: Guess what follows each opener.
Each student says one true story opener with a time phrase: 'Last summer, there was...'
tips: If a student says 'Before two days', note it and come back to it in the Arabic Bridge stage.
Keep the pace fast; this is a hook.

stages.name: Linguistics Corner: Climb the Story Mountain
stages.purpose: Learn the five parts of narrative structure and find them in a model story.
teacherSays: Draw a mountain on your paper with five flags. Flag 1 at the bottom left: setting. Flag 2 going up: rising action. Flag 3 at the top: climax. Flag 4 going down: falling action. Flag 5 at the bottom right: resolution.
A German writer, Gustav Freytag, drew this shape in 1863. Aristotle said it simpler, 2,300 years ago: beginning, middle, end.
Now listen to Hamad's true story, 'The Lost Ticket'. Which part is each sentence? Put your finger on the flag.
And the linguist William Labov found something else: real people add why the story matters. 'It was the most stressful day of my life!' That makes listeners care.
teacherSaysAr: ارسم جبلاً عليه خمس رايات: التمهيد، تصاعد الأحداث، الذروة، انحدار الأحداث، الخاتمة.
استمع إلى قصة حمد واجعل إصبعك على الراية المناسبة لكل جملة.
studentsDo: Draw the five-flag mountain.
Listen to and read 'The Lost Ticket' and label each sentence with a flag number.
Underline the linking words in the story (Last Friday, First, so, When, Suddenly, In the end).

exercise.instructions: Read each sentence from 'The Lost Ticket'. Which part of the mountain is it? 1 setting, 2 rising action, 3 climax, 4 falling action, 5 resolution.
exercise.instructionsAr: اقرأ كل جملة من قصة «التذكرة المفقودة». في أي جزء من الجبل هي؟ 1 التمهيد، 2 تصاعد الأحداث، 3 الذروة، 4 انحدار الأحداث، 5 الخاتمة.

items.prompt: Last Friday, there was a big football match in the city. Hamad and Omar had two tickets and they were very excited.
First, they took the bus, but there was a lot of traffic, so they were late.
When they arrived at the stadium, there was a long queue.
Suddenly, Hamad checked his pocket. His ticket wasn't there!
They ran back to the bus stop. The bus driver found the ticket on a seat and gave it back.
In the end, they watched the match and their team won. It was unforgettable!
Now Hamad always checks his pocket twice!

tips: Rising action can have several sentences; that is normal and a good discussion point.
Ask: 'Where is the feeling?' (very excited, unforgettable). Labov's evaluation is often hidden in adjectives from Lesson 4.

stages.name: Arabic Bridge: Openers, Endings and Ropes
stages.purpose: Use Arabic story knowledge as a tool and fix the translation traps (before two days, in last week, because... so).
teacherSays: Arabic grammar is clever here. What is the difference between 'دخل فجلس' and 'دخل ثم جلس'? With فـ he sat down immediately. With ثم there was some time. English uses words for this: then, immediately, after that, later.
Trap 1: قبل يومين. Many students say 'before two days'. English flips it: two days ago. The time first, then ago.
Trap 2: في الأسبوع الماضي. English: just 'last week'. No 'in'!
Trap 3: لأنني كنت متعباً فنمت. In English: ONE rope only. 'Because I was tired, I slept.' or 'I was tired, so I slept.'
Let's match Arabic and English story ropes.
teacherSaysAr: الفاء للتعقيب (فوراً)، وثم للتراخي (بعد مدة). والإنجليزية تعبّر عن ذلك بكلمات مثل immediately و after that و later.
قبل يومين = two days ago، والأسبوع الماضي = last week بلا in، واستخدم أداة ربط واحدة: because أو so.
studentsDo: Match the Arabic expressions with their English partners.
Say each English phrase in a sentence about their week.
Spot the trap: say which items would be wrong if translated word by word.

exercise.instructions: Match the Arabic with the best English. Watch out for word-by-word traps!
exercise.instructionsAr: صِل العبارة العربية بأفضل مقابل إنجليزي. احذر فخاخ الترجمة الحرفية!

items.prompt: كان يا ما كان، في قديم الزمان
items.answer: Once upon a time / A long time ago

items.prompt: قبل يومين
في الأسبوع الماضي
وفجأةً
وفي النهاية
لأنه كان هناك زحام
items.answer: because there was a lot of traffic

items.prompt: لذلك تأخرنا
وعاشوا في سعادة إلى الأبد
items.answer: and they lived happily ever after

tips: The فـ / ثم point impresses teens who study Arabic grammar at school; keep it to one example.
Do not say Arabic 'has no punctuation'; say Arabic style accepts longer chains with و.

stages.name: The Rope Workshop: Linking Words in Action
stages.nameAr: ورشة الحبال: كلمات الربط في العمل
stages.method: Guided practice: cloze with choices + reason talk
stages.purpose: Choose the right linking word for time, surprise, reason and result.
teacherSays: Here is Noor's story with missing ropes. Each rope has a job: time order, surprise, reason, result or ending.
Before you choose, ask: what is the job here?
Then read the whole story aloud with your rope. Does it flow?
teacherSaysAr: لكل كلمة ربط وظيفة: ترتيب زمني، مفاجأة، سبب، نتيجة أو خاتمة. اسأل نفسك أولاً: ما الوظيفة هنا؟
studentsDo: Complete the gaps (type in the chat or write on paper).
Name the job of each linking word.
Read the completed story aloud, one sentence each.

exercise.instructions: Complete Noor's story with: ago, there were, first, then, suddenly, because, so, in the end.
exercise.instructionsAr: أكمل قصة نور بالكلمات: ago, there were, first, then, suddenly, because, so, in the end.

items.prompt: Two weeks ___, Noor went to a school science fair.
___ a lot of students and parents in the hall.
___, she set up her volcano project on the table.
___ she explained it to the judges.
___, the volcano exploded too early!
It happened ___ she put in too much vinegar.
The table was wet, ___ she cleaned it quickly.
___, the judges laughed and gave her a special prize.

tips: Accept 'Finally' for the last gap and 'Next' for gap 4 and discuss small differences.
Point out the comma after First, Suddenly, In the end at the start of a sentence.

stages.name: Story Surgeons: Put It Back in Order
stages.method: Text reconstruction (jigsaw sentences) with cohesion clues
stages.purpose: Use linking words and the mountain shape as clues to order a story.
teacherSays: Oh no! Ziad's story fell off the mountain. The sentences are mixed up.
Your clues: time words, 'suddenly', 'so', 'in the end', and the mountain. Which sentence is the setting? Which is the climax?
Teams of two: you have 3 minutes. Then explain one clue that helped you.
teacherSaysAr: قصة زياد سقطت من الجبل وتبعثرت جملها! استخدم كلمات الربط وشكل الجبل لترتيبها.
studentsDo: Order the 8 sentences A-H (drag on the whiteboard or write the letters).
Explain one clue: 'C is first because it has the setting: Last summer, there was...'
Read the story in the right order.

exercise.instructions: Put the sentences of Ziad's story in the right order (1-8).
exercise.instructionsAr: رتّب جمل قصة زياد بالترتيب الصحيح (1-8).

items.prompt: A. Suddenly, there was a loud noise and the lights went out.
B. After that, we went to the gift shop and I bought a dinosaur key ring.
C. Last summer, there was a new dinosaur museum in our city, and my class visited it.
D. In the end, it was my favourite school trip ever.
E. First, we watched a short film about dinosaurs.
F. A minute later, the lights came on again. It was only a storm, so everyone laughed.
G. Then we walked around and saw a huge T. rex.
H. Everyone screamed because it was very dark.

tips: B and G could swap in theory; accept a different order if the student gives a logical reason.
This activity works well on the Teams Whiteboard with sticky notes.

stages.name: Team Creation: The Chain Story Mountain
stages.method: Collaborative storytelling (chain story) with story dice prompts
stages.purpose: Produce a whole story together, each student building one part of the mountain with the right linking words.
teacherSays: Now you are the writers. I roll the Story Dice: we get a place, a problem and a twist.

Student 1 builds the setting: 'Last ___, there was/were...'. Student 2 builds the rising action: 'First... then... so...'. Student 3 is the climax: 'Suddenly...!'. Student 4 fixes it and ends it: 'Because... In the end... It was...'
Each part: two or three sentences. Use past verbs and at least two linking words.
Then we swap roles and roll again!
teacherSaysAr: أرمي حجر القصة فنحصل على مكان ومشكلة ومفاجأة. كل طالب يبني جزءاً من الجبل بجملتين أو ثلاث وبكلمتي ربط على الأقل.
ثم نتبادل الأدوار ونرمي من جديد!
studentsDo: Roll (or choose) a story card set and plan their part for 1 minute.
Tell the story in a chain, one part each; the teacher types it on the whiteboard.
Swap roles and make a second story with new cards.
Vote for the best climax sentence.

exercise.instructions: Use the dice cards. Build one part of the story with 2-3 sentences and at least two linking words.
exercise.instructionsAr: استخدم بطاقات الحجر. ابنِ جزءاً من القصة بجملتين أو ثلاث وكلمتي ربط على الأقل.

items.prompt: Place: a crowded mall / Problem: a lost phone / Twist: a strange message
items.answer: Model: Last weekend, there were hundreds of people at the mall... Suddenly, my phone wasn't in my bag!

items.prompt: Place: a desert camp / Problem: a sandstorm / Twist: a surprise visitor
items.answer: Model: Last winter, my family went to a desert camp... Suddenly, there was a sandstorm...

items.prompt: Place: the school sports day / Problem: a broken shoe / Twist: a prize
items.answer: Model: Two weeks ago, there was a sports day at school... In the end, I won a prize!

items.prompt: Place: a birthday dinner / Problem: a long delay / Twist: the cake fell
items.answer: Model: Yesterday, it was my grandma's birthday... the food was late because there was a problem in the kitchen...

items.prompt: Place: a football match / Problem: heavy traffic / Twist: a famous player
items.answer: Model: Last Friday, there was a big match... there was a lot of traffic, so we were late...

items.prompt: Place: a library / Problem: a noisy group / Twist: a hidden message in a book
items.answer: Model: A few days ago, the library was quiet... Suddenly, I found an old note inside a book!

tips: Answers are models: any logical story with correct parts and linking words is right.
Give the climax student a dramatic voice tip: pause before 'Suddenly...'.
With fewer than 4 students, one student does both falling action and resolution.

stages.name: Exit Ticket, Shahrazad's Cliffhanger and Goodbye
stages.nameAr: بطاقة الخروج ونهاية شهرزاد المعلّقة والوداع
stages.purpose: Check the key ideas individually and end with a cliffhanger technique students can use.
teacherSays: Exit ticket: five questions. Answer in the chat.

Did you know? The most famous storyteller in the world is Arab: Shahrazad in 'One Thousand and One Nights'. Every night she stopped at the most exciting part. And Shahrazad... was overtaken by morning, and she stopped her story. 'وأدرك شهرزادَ الصباحُ فسكتت عن الكلام المباح.' That is a cliffhanger!
Your homework: write a story that stops at the climax. Next class, your friends will guess the ending!
teacherSaysAr: هل تعلم؟ أشهر راوية في العالم عربية: شهرزاد في «ألف ليلة وليلة». كانت تتوقف كل ليلة عند أكثر الأجزاء إثارة: «وأدرك شهرزادَ الصباحُ فسكتت عن الكلام المباح». هذه هي النهاية المعلّقة!
studentsDo: Answer the 5 exit-ticket items.
Say one cliffhanger sentence: 'Suddenly, I opened the door and...'
tips: Use the remaining minutes for the cliffhanger sentences; students love them.
Note anyone still saying 'before two days' for a quick recycle in Lesson 9.

items.prompt: Put in order: climax, setting, resolution, rising action, falling action
items.answer: setting, rising action, climax, falling action, resolution

items.prompt: 'Suddenly, the lights went out!' Which part of the mountain is it usually?
English for كان يا ما كان
Correct it: Before three days I visited my cousin.
items.answer: Three days ago I visited my cousin.

items.prompt: Correct it: Because it was raining, so we stayed home.
items.answer: Because it was raining, we stayed home. / It was raining, so we stayed home.

homework.en: The Shahrazad Challenge: write a true or invented story (100-120 words) that climbs the mountain but STOPS at the climax. Use there was/were, a time phrase, at least four linking words and one 'because' or 'so'. Draw the mountain and write which sentence goes with each flag.
homework.ar: تحدي شهرزاد: اكتب قصة حقيقية أو خيالية (100-120 كلمة) تصعد الجبل لكنها تتوقف عند الذروة. استخدم there was/were وعبارة زمن وأربع كلمات ربط على الأقل و because أو so. ارسم الجبل واكتب أي جملة تقع عند كل راية.
tasks: Highlight every linking word in one colour.
Write two possible endings on a separate paper; your classmates will guess next time.

support: Use a three-part mountain first (beginning, problem, ending), then split it into five.
Give a sentence frame for each flag: Last ___, there was... / First... then... / Suddenly... / ... so ... / In the end, it was...
In the chain story, let the student choose the part they feel safest with (often the setting).
challenge: Add Labov's 'evaluation': one sentence that says why the story matters, in the middle of the story, not only at the end.
Retell 'The Lost Ticket' from the bus driver's point of view.
Use 'meanwhile' to show two places at the same time (Meanwhile, at the stadium...).

successCriteria: Labels at least 6 of 7 sentences of 'The Lost Ticket' with the right mountain part.
Orders Ziad's story correctly or with a logical, explained variation.
Uses at least two different linking words correctly in their chain-story part.

teacherNotes: This class teaches structure, not new vocabulary: every story uses words from Lessons 1-8.
The mountain is a thinking tool, not a law: many great stories bend it. Say so to strong students.
Keep the Arabic examples respectful and light: folk tale formulas and Shahrazad are shared heritage the students can be proud of.
Bonus Class 3 adds the 'background' layer to the setting: was/were + -ing (It was raining...).
